source.name: QGIS Training Manual
source.note: Paraphrased exercise goals and factual operation mappings; no private workbook material.

selection.ordering: sha256(seed:id) within step count; unique operations only; alternating splits
selection.note: Repeated-tool exercises and four-step cases needing SQL arguments are outside this first method-only bench.

cases.goal: Find the places that satisfy both conditions at once: less than 50 m from a road and within 1 km of a school.
cautions: The school criterion is direct-line distance, not travel distance by road.

cases.goal: Limit my study area to the districts of Bellville, Cape, Goodwood, Kuils River, Mitchells Plain, Simon Town and Wynberg.

inputs.role: administrative districts with a NAME_2 name field

cautions: District names must match the attribute values exactly (e.g. 'Simon Town', 'Kuils River'); listing the field's values avoids typos.
An IN list and a chain of OR comparisons are equivalent.

cases.goal: Of the candidate buildings (all larger than 100 square metres), which ones touch the land we found to be suitable terrain? Give me them as a new layer.

inputs.role: candidate buildings from the earlier vector analysis (over 100 m2)

cautions: An intersection cuts the buildings along the terrain boundary: the output geometries are pieces of buildings, not whole buildings.
Touching suitable terrain is not the same as lying on it.
cases.source_section: Try Yourself (combine buildings with suitable terrain)

cases.goal: Convert three shapefiles in a folder to ED50 / UTM zone 29N (EPSG:23029) in one go, each saved under a name derived from the input name.
cautions: Output filenames must differ per row; build them from the input layer name.

cases.goal: Are my random sample points clustered, evenly spread or randomly scattered? Give me the summary measure and its significance.
cautions: The result depends on the study area implied by the layer extent and on the CRS units of the distances.
cases.source_section: Follow Along: Nearest Neighbor Analysis (within layer)

cases.goal: Pick out the major roads from the road table in the database and put the result on the map as a layer named roads_primary.

inputs.role: lines table in the PostGIS database

cautions: A query result can only be loaded as a layer if you name a column with unique integer values and the geometry column
cases.source_section: Follow Along: Executing SQL Queries with DB Manager

cases.goal: From the elevations measured at 100 scattered points, build a continuous elevation surface to get an idea of the terrain, weighting nearby points strongly (power 5).
cautions: 100 sample points are too few for a detailed terrain surface: the result is only a general and potentially misleading picture.
The Z field must be set explicitly in the advanced parameters.

cases.goal: Among the buildings that overlap suitable terrain, which ones only partly sit on it and should therefore be ruled out?
cautions: Buildings that were sliced by the intersection lie only partly on suitable terrain, so only part of the property is suitable; they should be eliminated.

cases.goal: Turn the 0-360 degree facing-direction map into four classes: 1 north (0-45 and 315-360), 2 east (45-135), 3 south (135-225), 4 west (225-315).

inputs.role: aspect in degrees derived from the dem

cautions: North spans the 0/360 wrap, so it needs two table rows mapping to the same class (5 rows for 4 classes).
How shared boundary values (45, 135, ...) are assigned depends on the 'Range boundaries' setting; check it.
Doing this with the raster calculator is possible but the expression becomes very long.

cases.goal: How long is the boundary of the Queensland region, and how large is its area?
cautions: Results are in the units of the layer CRS (and squared units for area)

cases.goal: Of the houses already close to a road and a school, keep only those that are also within 500 m of a restaurant.
cautions: Restaurants must be in the projected (metric) layer, otherwise 500 is not metres.
cases.source_section: Try Yourself: Further Filter our Buildings

cases.goal: List, without repeats, the town names of all buildings that lie in the Queensland region.
Simplify the facing-direction map into just four categories, north = 1, east = 2, south = 3, west = 4, using a rules file.
cautions: Aspect runs 0 (north) through 90, 180, 270 to 360 (north again), so north needs rules on both ends of the range.
Read the tool's manual tab for the exact rule syntax.

cases.goal: Keep only the candidate buildings that sit inside large continuous patches of suitable terrain, i.e. where suitable ground extends at least 100 m in every direction, and save them as the final answer.
cautions: A negative buffer distance shrinks the polygons (interior buffer); what remains is ground with suitable terrain for 100 m around it.
The distance is in metres only because the project uses a projected CRS; in a geographic CRS the same number would be degrees.

Selecting buildings that intersect the shrunken layer still keeps buildings that extend partly outside it; the manual accepts them because they lie within the original suitable terrain, so check containment against the original layer if 'entirely within' is the real requirement.
The 100 m threshold is a heuristic loosely tied to the 'over 100 m2' building size; the units (metres vs square metres) are not the same quantity.

cases.goal: Which buildings lie inside the KwaZulu region? Keep the answer as a layer I can show on the map.
cautions: A view loaded as a layer needs the gid key and the geometry column in its select list

cases.goal: Work out the floor-plan area of each candidate house in square metres and keep only those of at least 100 m2.
cautions: The area is in square metres only because the layer is in a projected CRS in metres.
Edits made with the field calculator must be saved (toggle editing off) before filtering.
The manual's criterion says 'more than 100' but the filter uses >= 100: decide whether the boundary value is included.
cases.source_section: Follow Along: Select Buildings of the Right Size

cases.goal: Give me the elevation statistics (min, max, mean, etc.) inside one particular sub-basin of my watershed map.
cautions: The clip uses only the selected polygon; without a selection all polygons are used.

cases.goal: Derive each city's boundary from where its residents live: the tightest outline without inward bends around all its addresses, widened by a margin, stored in a new table of areas.
cautions: The manual's answer stops at the convex hull and never applies the buffer it asks for
The answer replaces city_id with a row number, which matches the real city ids only if they are consecutive from 1
A city with fewer than three distinct addresses gives a point or line, which the polygon constraint rejects
In WGS 84 a buffer distance is in degrees

cases.goal: For each town name, draw the smallest outline without inward bends that encloses all buildings with that name, numbered in order of town name.
cautions: A group with fewer than three distinct points yields a point or a line, not a polygon

cases.goal: Find every region other than Hokkaido that comes within 100 metres of Hokkaido, so that small gaps or slivers in the borders do not hide a neighbour.
cautions: The 100 is in the layer CRS units; it means metres only because this data is projected
Hokkaido itself intersects its own zone and must be excluded
